featured_reviews.name: SPG
featured_reviews.review_text:
SBI Life Insurance – Great at selling dreams, terrible at delivering promises

The experience with SBI Life has been both deeply disappointing and troubling. Insurance products often fail to align with customers’ actual financial needs and fall far short of the standards expected by India’s Finance Ministry and IRDAI. Policy terms remain vague, opaque, and heavily skewed in the company’s favour, with virtually no transparency throughout the process.
Sales practices inside SBI branches remain highly aggressive and are frequently described by customers as predatory. Vulnerable groups — NRIs visiting for a short time, senior citizens, salaried employees in a hurry, and first-time investors with limited financial knowledge — are routinely targeted with intense high-pressure tactics. Policies are inadequately explained, long-term implications and charges are downplayed or glossed over, and customers typically discover the true (and far less favourable) picture only after the free-look period has expired — by which time it is usually too late to cancel without heavy loss.
Basic governance and due diligence at the point of sale are consistently lacking: full policy documents and accurate benefit illustrations are still, in 2025, regularly handed over only after the premium has been paid. When customers later highlight discrepancies, staff almost always shift the blame back to the policyholder for “not reading carefully” — a response that appears to enjoy silent approval from higher up the chain.
Attempts to surrender or exit are met with intimidating warnings of massive financial penalties through hidden clauses and deductions that were never clearly disclosed during the sale.
The grievance redressal mechanism is equally flawed—slow, biased, and marked by indifference and lack of professionalism. Staff often appear poorly trained and more focused on hitting sales targets and protecting personal incentives than resolving genuine concerns. Escalation of every single gatekeeper (Compliance, Risk, HR, Internal Ombudsman, Grievance Cell, Company Secretary, Customer Service, COO, CEO, Chairman) has seen mountains of proof and chosen either total silence or copy-paste nonsense replies. Hierarchy beats evidence every single time. Issues and grievances are routinely dismissed or met with silence, while erring employees are shielded and complainants are directed to external bodies—clearly prioritizing reputation management over actual justice.
Despite loudly promoting a “Customer First” philosophy and boasting “only 0.02 % mis-selling” in their 2024-25 Annual Report, SBI Life’s day-to-day operations still reflect a culture driven by sales quotas, internal cover-ups, and profit at the expense of people.
Once your money is with SBI Life, you are left vulnerable in a system that consistently places profits far above ethical service or customer well-being.
My strong advice: avoid SBI Life unless you enjoy fighting for years to get what is rightfully yours. Demand every document in advance, record every conversation, use the full free-look period, and seriously consider cleaner insurers instead.
Leadership: glossy reports and awards won’t rebuild the trust you have lost with millions of ordinary Indians.
